title: Kinematics Module 7 Lesson 1: Piecewise Continuity Find Constants custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with velocity $v(t) = k t\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 4$, and $v(t) = 20 - 2t\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $4 \le t \le 10$. Given that there is no sudden change in velocity at $t = 4\text{ s}$, find the value of $k$.

The acceleration of a particle is modelled by $a(t) = 2t + c\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $0 \le t \le 3$, and $a(t) = 15 - t\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $3 \le t \le 8$. Given that acceleration is continuous at $t = 3\text{ s}$, find the value of $c$.

A particle starts from rest at $t = 0$ with acceleration $a(t) = k t\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $0 \le t \le 5$, where $k$ is a constant. Given that its velocity at $t = 5\text{ s}$ is $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the value of $k$.

A particle moves with constant velocity $v(t) = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 5$, and then with velocity $v(t) = 2t - 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $t \ge 5$. Given that the displacement at $t = 5\text{ s}$ is $s(5) = 20\text{ m}$, find the displacement function $s(t)$ for $t \ge 5$.

A particle's velocity is given by $v(t) = p t^2 - q t\text{ m s}^{-1}$, where $p$ and $q$ are positive constants. The acceleration is zero when $t = 3\text{ s}$, and $v(3) = -9\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the values of $p$ and $q$.

The velocity of a particle is given by $v(t) = 18 - 2t\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 3$, and $v(t) = k t^2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $t \ge 3$. Given that there is no instantaneous change in velocity at $t = 3\text{ s}$, find the value of $k$.

questions.prompt:
A particle $P$ moves in a straight line from a fixed origin $O$. Its velocity $v\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at time $t\text{ s}$ is given by:
$$v(t) = \begin{cases} 4t & \text{for } 0 \le t \le 3 \\ k(t - 7)^2 & \text{for } 3 \le t \le 7 \end{cases}$$
where $k$ is a constant. There is no sudden change in velocity at $t = 3\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that $k = 0.75$, and find the time at which the particle comes to rest.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the displacement of $P$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$, and find the total distance travelled by $P$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 7\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: A particle starts from rest at the origin $O$ at $t = 0$. For $0 \le t \le 6$, its acceleration is given by $a(t) = k(36 - t^2)\text{ m s}^{-2}$, where $k$ is a positive constant. Given that the velocity of the particle at $t = 6\text{ s}$ is $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the value of $k$, and write down the expression for $v(t)$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the displacement of the particle from $O$ at $t = 6\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt:
A particle moves in a straight line from a fixed origin $O$. Its velocity $v\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is given by:
$$v(t) = \begin{cases} p t^2 - q t & \text{for } 0 \le t \le 6 \\ 63 - 4.5t & \text{for } 6 \le t \le 14 \end{cases}$$
where $p$ and $q$ are positive constants. There are no instantaneous changes in velocity, and the acceleration of the particle is zero when $t = 2\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Form two simultaneous equations in $p$ and $q$, and solve them to find the values of $p$ and $q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum velocity of the particle during the first phase $0 \le t \le 6$, and find its displacement at $t = 6\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ travels in a straight line from $A$ to $B$. The velocity $v\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at time $t\text{ s}$ after leaving $A$ is given by $v(t) = 0.04t^3 + c t^2 + k t$, where $c$ and $k$ are constants. Particle $P$ takes $5\text{ s}$ to travel from $A$ to $B$, reaching $B$ with speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The distance $AB$ is $25\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that $5c + k = 1$ and $250c + 75k = 112.5$, and solve these equations to find the values of $c$ and $k$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Obtain an expression for the acceleration $a(t)$, and show that the acceleration of $P$ attains its minimum value at $t = 2.5\text{ s}$, finding this minimum acceleration.

questions.prompt:
A particle moves in a straight line starting from rest at $O$ ($s(0) = 0, v(0) = 0$). Its acceleration is modelled by:
$$a(t) = \begin{cases} 6 - 1.5t & \text{for } 0 \le t \le 4 \\ k & \text{for } 4 \le t \le 8 \end{cases}$$
where $k$ is a constant. The particle comes to instantaneous rest at $t = 8\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the velocity and displacement of the particle at $t = 4\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the constant acceleration $k$ in the second phase, and find the total distance travelled by the particle from $t = 0$ to $t = 8\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt:
A particle moves in a straight line starting from the origin $O$ at $t = 0$. Its velocity is modelled by:
$$v(t) = \begin{cases} p t^2 + q t & \text{for } 0 \le t \le 4 \\ 24 - 2t & \text{for } 4 \le t \le 12 \end{cases}$$
where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Both velocity and acceleration are continuous at the transition $t = 4\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By applying the continuity conditions for velocity and acceleration at $t = 4\text{ s}$, show that $p = -1.5$ and find the value of $q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum velocity of the particle, the time $t$ at which it comes to rest, and the total distance travelled from $t = 0$ to when it comes to rest.

questions.prompt:
A train moves along a straight horizontal track from station $A$ to station $B$, starting from rest at $t = 0$ and stopping at $t = 30\text{ s}$. Its velocity $v\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is modelled by:
$$v(t) = \begin{cases} c t^2 & \text{for } 0 \le t \le 10 \\ V & \text{for } 10 \le t \le 22 \\ m(30 - t) & \text{for } 22 \le t \le 30 \end{cases}$$
where $c, V$, and $m$ are constants. The velocity is continuous throughout the motion, and the total distance between stations $A$ and $B$ is $580\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express $c$ and $m$ in terms of $V$, and show that the distance travelled in the first phase is $\frac{10}{3}V$ and in the third phase is $4V$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the total distance of $580\text{ m}$, find the cruise speed $V$, the value of $c$, the deceleration $m$, and the acceleration of the train at $t = 5\text{ s}$.
